title: 중국 이혼 재산분할에서 디지털자산 규제에 대한 검토와 제언
journal: The Journal of China Area Studies

title: When AI meets design: the role of enhanced and impeded human–AI interaction in designers’ value co-creation
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose With the rapid penetration of generative AI (GAI) in product design, designer-GAI value co-creation has emerged as a transformative new paradigm. However, the drivers and inhibitors of professional designers’ intentions to engage in GAI value co-creation remain under-explored, especially from the designer-centric perspective. Grounded in parasocial interaction theory (PSI), this study aims to examine how heterogeneous human–AI interaction modes (enhanced vs. impeded) affect designers’ co-creation intentions. Design/methodology/approach This study examines the hypotheses using survey data from 305 professional designers analyzed via partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Results show that the informativeness and novelty of GAI outputs significantly and positively predict designers’ co-creation intentions. Enhanced human–AI interaction positively promotes both informativeness and novelty, with AI transparency positively moderating these effects. Impeded human–AI interaction only negatively affects informativeness, with no significant effect on novelty, and AI transparency shows no moderating effect here. Originality/value This study extends human–AI interaction research and provides actionable guidance for GAI application in design practice.

title: USING SINUSOIDAL INSTEAD OF TRIANGULAR STIMULUS SIGNALS ON THE IEEE 1057 STANDARD RANDOM NOISE TEST OF ADCS
journal: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences
abstract: The random-noise test for analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) prescribed by the IEEE Standard 1057 for Digitizing Waveform Recorders relies on a triangular signal to stimulate the converter under test. This paper shows that a sinusoidal stimulus may be used in its place without changing the estimator. Doing so makes the test more flexible and, more importantly, opens the way to sine-fitting algorithms for recovering the initial phase of the two data records that the test requires. Once known, this initial phase allows the two records to be aligned, reducing the error that additive noise introduces through the acquisition trigger. It is proved that the estimator obtained for the sinusoidal case coincides with the one recommended by the standard for the triangular case, and the two are compared, together with the direct-current case, both analytically and through their expected values and errors.

title: The lived experience of self-compassion among participants in the Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) program: A hermeneutic phenomenological study
journal: Journal of Meditation based Psychological Counseling
abstract: Purpose: This study explored how adults who participated in a Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) program experience self-compassion, and interpreted the meaning structure of that experience to reveal its underlying essence. Methods: Van Manen’s hermeneutic phenomenology was adopted. Data were collected from three adults who had completed a standard MSC program through individual written accounts and two group in-depth interviews, and were analyzed through the four existentials of lived body, lived time, lived space, and lived relation. Results: Self-compassion was not a matter of acquiring a new skill or reaching a particular emotional state, but an existential experience of reorienting one’s relationship with oneself. It emerged as participants became aware of their present selves through bodily sensation; took shape over time through repeated wavering and returning; was fostered in a space where the pressures of evaluation and achievement were suspended; and unfolded as understanding oneself extended into understanding others. These four dimensions converged into a single movement, whose essence was interpreted as “a mind that turns back against the current”—a turning away from the familiar direction that had continually driven participants forward, and a return to the self as it is in the present. Conclusion: Self-compassion is understood not as a fixed psychological trait but as an existential way of being. Self-compassion-based programs should cultivate a safe environment in which the burdens of evaluation and achievement are suspended, and should respect participants’ life contexts and their own pace.

title: The drivers and inhibitors of resident participatory processes in places with a negative reputation
journal: Journal of Place Management and Development
abstract: Purpose This study explores the factors that drive or inhibit resident participation in place branding initiatives, particularly in places with a negative reputation. It aims to deepen the understanding of different participatory practices in contexts where place image challenges and socio-economic issues intersect. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a multidisciplinary framework combining insights from place branding, public administration and governance. It analyses three place branding campaigns in Luton, UK, using semi-structured interviews with residents and officials and netnographic analysis of online content. Findings The research identifies four major factors influencing participation: residents’ needs and benefits; campaign activities, recruitment and coordination; ownership, misrepresentation and power; and social tensions and lack of trust. The findings show that these factors do not operate as fixed drivers or inhibitors; rather, their role varies across top-down, bottom-up and mixed participatory approaches. Active participation is often driven by a desire to counter misrepresentation and foster community identity, whereas passive participation is more common in top-down initiatives with limited resident influence. Research limitations/implications This study is limited to one location with a negative reputation and may not be generalisable. Future studies should explore different cultural and spatial contexts to broaden the applicability of findings. Practical implications Effective resident participation requires addressing both intrinsic (ownership, trust) and extrinsic (professional benefits, coordination) motivators. Policymakers and place managers must design inclusive processes that balance control with community autonomy, particularly in stigmatised areas. Originality/value This study offers a novel, integrated view of resident participation by identifying how drivers and inhibitors interact across campaign types. It contributes original insights into participatory place branding in contexts of reputational and socio-economic disadvantage.

title: Sustainable hospital accreditation in low- and middle-income countries: lessons for global stakeholders from Sri Lanka's discontinued national program
journal: International Journal of Health Care Quality Assurance
abstract: Purpose Poor quality and unsafe healthcare exert an immense burden on resource-constrained health systems in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). Hospital accreditation programs (HAPs) can help address this challenge, but many programs are not sustained, and limited research explains why. This case study aimed to inform future HAP implementation by examining the emergence, progression and discontinuation of the Sri Lankan Hospital Accreditation Program (SLHAP). Design/methodology/approach Purposively selected accreditation stakeholders (n = 18), directly involved in the SLHAP, were interviewed using a validated, semi-structured guide. Data were thematically analysed, with coding validated. Findings The SLHAP emerged through strong government leadership, with international technical and financial assistance. It progressed through standard practices, including developing standards, surveyor training and compliance gap analysis, facilitated by robust organisational structures. Discontinuation was due to limitations in project management and in the integration of HAP elements, resulting from governance constraints and leadership turnover. This resulted in frequent changes of plans, delays in adapting and communicating standards, and limited awareness and competencies among stakeholders. Practical implications A complex interaction of myriad factors produced the SLHAP's trajectory. The primary factors found to have led to discontinuation (project management, leadership turnover and governance constraints) can be addressed prospectively in other LMICs through comprehensive, effective and long-term project planning and management. Originality/value This study offers an in-depth exploration of meso- and micro-level factors shaping the overall trajectory of SLHAP, highlighting the importance of strengthening project management and meticulous integration of HAP elements. Therefore, SLHAP gives a unique opportunity to learn from a discontinued HAP in an LMIC.

title: Study on the Relationship Between the Evolution of Blue-Green Space Landscape Patterns and Surface Temperature Changes in the Downtown Area of Jingzhou
journal: Compendium of Earth and Space Sciences 地球與空間科學輯要
abstract: 【Objective】To explore the evolution of urban blue-green space landscape patterns and their relationship with changes in land surface temperature, providing reference for the optimization of urban blue-green spaces. 【Methods】Taking the central urban area of Jingzhou as the study area, based on land use data and Landsat remote sensing images from 2005, 2015, and 2025, eight landscape pattern indicators, including PLAND, PD, LPI, LSI, COHESION, DIVISION, SHDI, and AI, were selected to analyze the evolution characteristics of blue-green space landscape patterns. Combined with the results of land surface temperature retrieval, global Moran's I, local Moran's I, and correlation analysis methods were used to explore the relationship between landscape pattern changes and land surface temperature changes. 【Results】(1) From 2005 to 2025, the proportion and dominant patch size of blue-green spaces in the central urban area of Jingzhou continuously decreased, with PLAND and LPI dropping from 85.67% and 84.30% to 71.35% and 68.24%, respectively, while PD, LSI, and DIVISION showed continuous increases, indicating increasing fragmentation of blue-green spaces. (2) Land surface temperature exhibited obvious spatial differentiation, with high-temperature areas mainly distributed in densely built-up regions, and rivers, water bodies, and concentrated green areas showing lower temperatures. The changes in blue-green spaces corresponded well spatially with the changes in land surface temperature. (3) Spatial autocorrelation analysis showed that changes in blue-green space landscape patterns and land surface temperature exhibited significant spatial clustering and local correlation features. (4) PLAND, LPI, COHESION, and AI were negatively correlated with changes in land surface temperature, while PD, LSI, DIVISION, and SHDI were positively correlated, with PLAND having the highest correlation. 【Conclusion】The changes in blue-green space patterns in the central urban area of Jingzhou are significantly associated with changes in land surface temperature. Increasing the scale, integrity, and connectivity of blue-green spaces helps enhance cooling effects, while landscape fragmentation weakens their thermal environment regulation capabilities. Future urban development should strengthen the protection of blue-green spaces and the construction of connectivity networks, reducing the fragmentation of ecological spaces caused by construction activities.

title: Servant leadership effect on knowledge-hiding behavior: the moderated mediation influence of hope and burnout
abstract: Purpose This study examines the mechanisms and boundary conditions underlying the relationship between servant leadership and knowledge-hiding behavior, using a moderated mediation model based on data from Indian employees across diverse industries. Design/methodology/approach A total of 311 valid responses was analyzed employing Hayes’s PROCESS macro to test the proposed model. Findings Hope moderates the relationship between servant leadership and burnout. Specifically, servant leadership is associated with the strongest negative indirect effect on knowledge-hiding through burnout when hope is low. This negative effect persists but weakens when hope is high. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design restricts causal interpretations. Practical implications Findings offer insights to help organizations reduce knowledge-hiding behaviors among employees. Originality/value This study advances servant leadership and knowledge-hiding research by identifying how situational factors such as hope influence the effectiveness of servant leadership, emphasizing the need to align leadership style with contextual conditions to optimize outcomes.
